A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same COPE study. Their main text, equations, tables, figures, and complete appendices support reliable comparison despite changed pagination and table numbering.

before.justification: V4 reports original benchmark experiments on mathematical reasoning, code generation, open-ended generation, and ALFWorld, alongside appendix ablations and repeated-run results.

after.justification: V5 retains those original experiments and adds planning controls, failure and conditional-cost analyses, and repeated-run AIME-2024 results.

M1.justification: COPE retains the same three-stage planner/executor cascade, plan reuse, sampling, and task-specific routing procedures. The new planning variants are experimental controls rather than changes to the proposed method.

E1.justification: Both versions evaluate MATH-500, AIME-2024, MBPP with MBPP-ET hidden tests, MT-Bench, and ALFWorld. Renaming 'agent tasks' to 'sequential decision-making' clarifies the existing coverage without introducing a new task or environment.

E2.justification: Section 5.5 and Table 8 add No-plan cascade, Plan-only, Verify-only, and Self-plan to the planning comparison. The original benchmark comparator sets, including Cascade, ABC, and FrugalGPT, remain unchanged.

E3.justification: The new planning experiments distinguish a full-cascade control preserving acceptance and escalation rules from single-stage planner/verifier alternatives and a large-only reference. The conditional-cost analysis compares methods on the same Stage-3 queries. Existing benchmark settings are retained; the additional cost-accounting and latency descriptions clarify existing measurements.

E4.justification: Beyond the retained truncation, difficulty, sampling, threshold, latency, and qualitative analyses, v5 adds controls isolating planning's contribution, high-consensus incorrect acceptances, and conditional cascading penalties. Section 5.5 and Appendices A.1.4/A.1.6 substantially strengthen examination of the central mechanism and its failure conditions.

E5.justification: V4 Table 13 reports MATH-500 means and standard deviations over five independent runs with different seeds. V5 Table 16 adds 95% confidence intervals and extends repeated-run reporting to AIME-2024. Five runs remain the stated count; an increase is not reported.

E6.justification: Tables 3–5 retain their numerical results, while Tables 6–7 correct swapped MT-Bench/ALFWorld score and cost blocks. Substantial new evidence includes No-plan cascade at 71.2% accuracy/265 cost versus COPE at 74.4%/212, 3.97% incorrect Stage-1 acceptances, a 1.25-fold conditional Stage-3 cost penalty, and repeated-run AIME results. These are added findings and attribution corrections, not improvements in retained benchmark scores.

T1.justification: Appendix A.2 corrects the objective from extracting the answer of the most probable solution trace to maximizing answer probability after aggregating traces. Equations 2, 4, and 5 now consistently describe answer-level marginalization and majority voting. The latent-plan decomposition and MoE analogy remain.

C1.justification: The introduction and conclusion narrow claims of matching or surpassing large models to comparable performance with lower paid API cost in the evaluated settings. Broad deployment claims are qualified by latency and final-stage cost penalties. The central contribution of training-free collaboration through planning is retained.

C2.justification: The new Limitations section explains uncalibrated routing signals, test-coverage and observability limits, excluded local computation costs, and unsuitable latency-sensitive applications. Results discussion tempers superiority claims using uncertainty estimates, and the broader-impact statement replaces a sustainability implication with an affordability claim. These substantially extend v4's narrower latency discussion.

D1.justification: Appendix A.3 replaces the supplementary-material code statement with a repository URL. V5 also clarifies that latency includes API/network time, qualifies the general GPU statement, and explicitly excludes local hardware and energy from paid API cost. Model versions, batch sizes, decoding temperatures, and prompts are retained.

R1.justification: The cited works remain the same after matching bibliographic updates. Section 2 removes the claim that, unlike prior work, COPE extends to open-ended and agent tasks, modestly narrowing its novelty positioning.

P1.justification: V5 makes targeted rewrites to the introduction, results, conclusion, and theoretical explanation; standardizes cost and task terminology; and adds planning-ablation, limitations, and acknowledgment sections. Most existing prose and the overall narrative order remain intact.

P2.justification: V5 adds three analysis tables and expands the uncertainty table with dataset blocks and confidence-interval columns. Journal headers and an expanded author block change pagination. Figures 1–5 are retained, with qualitative captions correcting 'left' to 'top' rather than rearranging the examples.

improvement.justification: V5 resolves important weaknesses in evidential support and reporting: planning controls test the central mechanism, Appendix A.2 corrects the voting formalization, and Tables 6–7 repair misassigned benchmark results. Confidence intervals and explicit routing, cost, and latency limitations also make the conclusions better supported. Together these substantially improve the paper's reliability and practical interpretability while retaining its core study.
